sentences.text:
Mr. Ali Imam Shah ,
 .... For the respondents.

The instant appeal has been preferred against the judgment and award dated September 29, 2021 passed by the learned Tribunal, Purba Burdwan , in M.A.C. case No. 27 of 20140/68 of 2010 The brief fact of the case is that the present respondent no.1

being the mother of the deceased has filed an application under Section 163A of the M.V. Act before the learned Tribunal for getting compensation from the Insurance Company on the ground her unmarried son was died in a road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle duly insured under the policy of the insurance company.
The claim was contested by the Insurance Company by filing written statement.
After hearing the parties, the learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.3,88,500/- in favour the respondent no.1.
Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned award, the insurance Company has preferred the instant appeal.
Learned advocate for the insurance Company submits that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger in the offending goods vehicle.
The owner has violated the terms of the policy.
Accordingly, the Insurance Company may not be liable to pay the compensation.

The learned Tribunal has considered the fact and is of opinion that in the case of gratuitous passenger, Insurance Company may be directed to pay the third party and then the same may be indemnified from owner; but has not passed any specific direction.
So he prayed for necessary modification of the order.

Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the claimant/respondent no.1 submits that that the learned Tribunal has considered the fact pleaded by the Insurance Company and has specified in his finding at inner page 11 of the impugned award.
But necessary order has not been passed.

sentences.text: Heard the learned advocates and perused the impugned award.

It appears that the learned Tribunal is of opinion that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger, the third party may be received the compensation from the insurance company, later it may be indemnified by the owner.
However, the operative portion of the impugned award, no such direction was made.
Considering the same, it appears that the instant appeal has got merit and the award passed by the learned Tribunal need be modified only to that effect.
Accordingly, the award passed by the learned Tribunal amounting to Rs.3,88,500/- hereby affirmed.
The Insurance Company is directed to pay compensation to the claimant together with 6% interest per annum from the date of filing of the claim application i.e. from 20.2.2015.

It appears that at the time of filing of the instant appeal, the Insurance Company has deposited the statutory sum of Rs.25,000/- vide OD Challan 2470 dated 17.3.2022 and later also deposited the amount of Rs.5,38,016/- vide OD Challan no.3363 dated 6.1.2023.
Accordingly, the Insurance Company has deposited total Rs.5,63,016/-, the same amount must have accrued some interest.

The office of the learned Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta is directed to disburse the amount along with accrued interest in name of the claimants within four weeks from the date of passing of this order according to the regular norms regarding identification, satisfaction etc.

After such deposit, the Insurance Company is at liberty to recover the entire amount of compensation from the owner of the offending vehicle i.e. respondent nos. 2 and 3 of this appeal accordingly to the procedure laid down by the Honble Supreme Court in National Insurance Vs. Chella Bharathamma.
Accordingly, FMAT(MV) 104 of 2022 is disposed of.
Connected applications, if any, are also disposed of.
All parties shall act on the server copy of this order duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.

( Subhendu Samanta, J.)
